SPECIFICATION FOR 

CARBIDE TIPPED CORE DRILLS WITH 

MORSE TAPER SHANKS 



1. Scope — Covers the dimensions and requirements for carbide tipped core drills with morse taper 
shanks. 

2. Dimensions — As given in Table 1. 

3. Tolerances — The tolerance on cutting length h and overall length /shall be as given below: 



Cutting Length \ % and Overall Length /

4. Material — Cutting Portion — Carbide tip. 

Shank and Body — Carbon steel with tensile strength not less than 1375 M Pa* 
beyond 30 mm from the end of carbide tip length. 

5. Hardness — Body — 430 HV Min beyond 25 mm from rear end of carbide tip 

Tany- 320 to 450 rW 

6. General Requirements 

6.1 Unless otherwise specified, core drills with right hand helical flutes for right hand cutting shall 
be supplied. 

6.2 The range of applications of carbide tips shall be K20 for cast iron and P30 for steel according 
to IS : 2428-1964 * Application of carbides for machining ranges of application and colour code \ 

6.3 Morse taper shanks according to IS : 1715-1973 ' Dimensions for self holding tapers '. 

6.4 Back taper shall be 0"02to 0'05 on diameter for 100 mm flute length. 

6.5 Carbide tips shall be according to IS : 9327-1979 ' Dimensions for carbide tips for reamers, core 
drills cind slot milling cutters \ 

6.6 Core Drills for Pre-fmishing Operations — When core drills are used for pre-flnishing operations, 
the following amount of stock removal is recommended and the diameters of the core drills shall be 
calculated accordingly:

7. Sampling — The sampling and criteria of acceptance shall be in accordance with IS : 7778-1975 
1 Methods for sampling small tools '. 

8. Designation — A carbide tipped core drill with morse taper shank tor right hand cutting having 
diameter d = 16 mm, carbide tip of range of application K20 and conforming to this standard, 
shall be designated as: 

CT Core Drill 16 IS : 9771 K20 

9. Marking — Shall be marked with the following: 

a) Diameter d } 

b) Range of application of carbide tip, and 

c) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 

The above markings shall be so applied and finished that it does not interfere with the 
secure holding of the drill. 

9.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

10. Protective Coating and Packing 

10.1 Each drill shall be covered with a suitable rust proofing material. 

10.2 The cutting portion of the drill shall be protected against damage by a suitable plastic coatirrg. 

10.3 Each drill or a number of drills shall be wrapped in non-absorbent paper and protected by a 
cover bearing the size, range of application of carbide tip and the manufacturer's name or trade- 
mark. 

10.4 Drills of only one size shall be packed in one carton. 

3 



IS : 9771 - 1981 

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from 
DIN 8044-1979 ' Aufbohrer mit Sehneidplatten aus Hartmetall ( Core drills with carbide tips ), issued 
by Deutsches Institut fur Normung. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
